target_customer: Latin American consumers and freelancers, starting in Colombia, who want to hold dollars to avoid peso devaluation
problem: Latin Americans lose savings to currency devaluation and have limited access to dollar accounts and international payments.
business_model: Consumer fintech: free tier plus paid Littio PRO membership, card interchange and yield spread on stablecoin-backed balances

founders.name: Christian Knudsen
founders.background_notes: YC page: over a decade scaling tech startups across fintech, agriculture and web3; Forbes Colombia says growth and marketing roles.

founders.name: Ivan Torroledo
prior_employers: Banco de la Republica de Colombia (central bank), early career per Forbes Colombia
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as physics and economics data scientist with 9+ years in banking and financial services.

founders.name: Luis Huertas
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by Forbes Colombia (2022-03); Valora Analitik calls him co-founder and CEO. Not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Wallet, card issuing partnerships, stablecoin rails and local payment integration (PSE, Nequi); regulatory structure matters more than raw engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Brand and card plus yield products help, but competitors such as DolarApp and local banks offer similar dollar accounts; Littio states it is not a bank and not supervised by the financial regulator.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Lulo Bank added a dollar savings feature (Lulo X) and DolarApp offered digital dollar accounts in Colombia; sources are undated for these moves.

market_need_then: Colombian peso devaluation and limited dollar access drove demand; a 2022 Forbes article frames the company around protecting Latin Americans from devaluation.

identity.mascot_or_character: Selenio, an in-app and WhatsApp virtual assistant
identity.voice_and_tone: Spanish-language consumer finance focused on dollars and yields

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage in Forbes, Portafolio and Valora Analitik; company states over 500,000 users (self-reported via Enter.co).

brand_strength.rationale: Regular regional press and a large claimed user base, but no sourced evidence about the brand itself driving growth; sources do not explain the name.

pivots.from: Dollar savings account and Mastercard debit in Colombia
pivots.to: Multi-currency stablecoin wallet (dollars, euros, pesos) with US ACH and European IBAN receiving and a regional expansion
pivots.why: Not stated; shown by the current product and press on Europe transfers and expansion.

outcome_analysis: Littio is active with 37 people on the YC page and claims over 500,000 users and expansion from Dubai plus other Latin American countries. It raised a $3.7M pre-seed in March 2022 led by 1662nd, and later reports cite about $4M to $4.5M total. Its model depends on stablecoin rails and operating outside bank supervision in Colombia, a regulatory risk rather than an observed failure.
notes: Pre-seed amount from Forbes Colombia (2022-03-10), cross-checked by Forbes Argentina saying about US$4 million received (a looser figure). Aggregators show $500K in 2023-04 and totals of $4.2M to $4.5M; those are unverified and not recorded as rounds. A 2026 announcement of Oscar Florez joining as co-founder and CPTO was seen only in a search snippet. Competitor sources found (Lulo X, DolarApp) are undated, so the dated competitor list is empty. Outcome search found no shutdown, layoffs or acquisition. Sources disagree on founding year (2021 per YC and CB Insights, 2023 per one aggregator).
